stories.headline: Trump and Anduril unveil a $6.6 billion ‘software-defined’ shipyard in Baltimore County to build Virginia-class submarine parts
stories.summary: The White House and Anduril Industries announced plans Tuesday for Arsenal-2, a shipyard of more than 2 million square feet on a 187-acre site at Tradepoint Atlantic in Sparrows Point, the old Bethlehem Steel property outside Baltimore, ahead of President Trump’s 4 PM visit there. The Navy has awarded Anduril a contract worth up to $2.9 billion, and the company will put in $3.7 billion of its own money. The White House says the $6.6 billion project will create more than 13,000 direct and indirect jobs. The yard will build Virginia-class submarine sections such as torpedo tubes, sterns and bow sections and ship them to Electric Boat in Groton, Connecticut, and Newport News Shipbuilding for final assembly. Anduril’s ArsenalOS software will run the production floor. Permitting starts now, and the first operations are expected in 2030. Maryland officials call it the largest single private investment in the state.

stories.headline: Treasury blocked $175 million in federal payments to dead people this fiscal year, nearly double the earlier count
stories.summary: The Treasury Department stopped about 13,500 federal payments worth $175 million that were headed to people who had died, up from $99 million identified just months earlier, Fox News Digital reports from figures released Tuesday. Treasury screened more than 1.1 billion federal payments totaling about $3.7 trillion in fiscal 2026, and more than 99% of federal programs can now check payments against its “Do Not Pay” system, up from about 4% a year ago. The expansion follows Trump’s March 2025 executive order on improper payments and Sen. John Kennedy’s Ending Improper Payments to Deceased People Act, which Trump signed in February to give Treasury permanent access to Social Security’s full death records. “We are moving beyond ‘pay and chase,’” Secretary Scott Bessent said. Kennedy’s line: “Unless you were playing Frisbee in the quad during Econ 101, you know the federal government shouldn’t be sending taxpayer money to dead people.”

stories.headline: Trumbull volleyball goes 9–0 with a four-set win at Southington; McMahon visits Tuesday
stories.summary: Trumbull High’s girls volleyball team stayed perfect with a 3–1 win at Southington on Friday (25–18, 25–20, 25–27, 25–17), its ninth straight victory to open the season, according to MaxPreps. Adriana Castillo led the Eagles with 18 kills, 12 digs and two aces, setter Lauren Yakowicz added 25 assists, six digs, four aces and two solo blocks, and Paulina Bykowski chipped in seven kills, six digs and six aces. Southington’s Lily Eidukaityte had 13 kills and 14 digs in the loss, which dropped the Blue Knights to 8–5. Trumbull has now won nine of its last 10 road matches and hosts Brien McMahon at 5:30 p.m. Tuesday. The win capped a week that also included 3–0 sweeps of Ridgefield and Stamford.

stories.headline: Insta360 X6 firmware 1.2.35 adds 4K120 360 video and a new 360 slow-motion mode at up to 4K200
stories.summary: Insta360’s latest firmware for the X6, version 1.2.35, is its first real feature update since the camera launched in August. The regular 360 Video mode now records 4K at 120 frames per second, and a new 360 Slow-Mo mode shoots 4K at 200, 120 or 100fps, so a jump, wave or dog running past can be reframed and slowed down after the fact; 200fps played back at 25fps is eight times slower. Flat video gains 24 and 48fps, flat photos get 4:3 and 3:4 shapes, and AI Director can now be limited to a date range. The update needs the Insta360 app 2.34.5 or later, and Insta360 Studio 6.0.6 on the desktop already supports the new slow-motion files. The catch: 4K spread around a full sphere looks softer once reframed than the X6’s 8K mode.

stories.headline: Kilmar Ábrego Garcia is back in federal court as the government pushes again to deport him to Liberia
stories.summary: The Justice Department is back before U.S. District Judge Paula Xinis in Maryland on Tuesday, asking her to lift the preliminary injunction that bars ICE from detaining Kilmar Ábrego Garcia and deporting him to Liberia. His lawyers want the order made permanent. The Salvadoran, who entered the U.S. illegally as a teenager and has an American wife and child, was wrongly sent to El Salvador’s CECOT prison in March 2025 and brought back in June 2025 to face a Tennessee human-smuggling charge. A judge threw that case out in May, finding it was brought to punish him, and the government is appealing. He says he will go to Costa Rica, which agreed to take him, but former acting ICE Director Todd Lyons wrote in March that sending him there would be “prejudicial” after the U.S. spent political capital getting Liberia to accept third-country deportees.

stories.headline: Paramount closes its $110 billion takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery, putting CBS News and CNN under David Ellison’s new ‘Skydance’
stories.summary: Paramount Skydance completed its $110 billion purchase of Warner Bros. Discovery on Tuesday, and the combined company is now called Skydance. It owns the Paramount and Warner Bros. film studios, CBS News and CNN, cable networks including Comedy Central, Nickelodeon, TBS and TNT, and the Paramount+ and HBO Max streaming services. David Ellison will run it with co-CEO Ynon Kreiz, the former Mattel chief. Warner shareholders get roughly $31 a share in cash. The deal closed after Paramount settled antitrust suits from 12 state attorneys general and the Writers Guild. Under that settlement it must make 30 films a year for the first two years and cannot sell or close the Paramount or Warner Bros. lots in Los Angeles for at least five years. “Today is a historic day,” Ellison said.

stories.headline: Hackers claim a Trump Mobile breach that exposed names, home addresses and phone numbers of about 3,600 customers
stories.summary: Trump Mobile appears to have suffered a data breach exposing information on 3,615 people, including names, home addresses, emails, phone numbers and order details, according to PCMag and Straight Arrow News, which reached several people in the leaked file who confirmed their data was accurate. Some had only started signing up and never finished. A group calling itself BYOD claimed responsibility, telling PCMag it got in by planting a remote-access trojan on a worker at Liberty Mobile, the carrier behind Trump Mobile’s network, and claiming access to the website’s back end. The file also reportedly includes information on Eric Brunnett, the Trump Organization’s chief information technology officer. Trump Mobile did not immediately answer requests for comment.

stories.headline: Germany arrests former spy chief August Hanning on suspicion of selling state secrets to a foreign service
stories.summary: German federal prosecutors on Tuesday arrested August Hanning, 80, who ran the BND foreign intelligence service from 1998 to 2005, on suspicion of treasonous espionage, spying out state secrets and attempted treason. A former aide identified as Manfred D., who was Hanning’s chief of staff and later served several BND presidents in the same job from 2012 until this year, was also arrested and charged with aiding and abetting. Prosecutors say the two agreed in 2010 that Manfred D. would keep passing valuable BND intelligence to Hanning in exchange for payment. Hanning was picked up in Bad Tölz-Wolfratshausen in Bavaria and his former aide in Steinfurt in western Germany. Prosecutors did not say which country’s intelligence service the secrets were allegedly meant for.

stories.headline: Drones hit merchant ships in the Black Sea, sinking one in Bulgaria’s waters in a first for the NATO member’s economic zone
stories.summary: Two merchant ships, the Togo-flagged Alfa Watan and the Palau-flagged Able, were struck by drones of unknown origin about 70 miles off Bulgaria’s coast on Tuesday, Bulgarian broadcaster Nova reported, the first reported drone attack on commercial shipping inside Bulgaria’s exclusive economic zone. The Alfa Watan suffered severe damage and sank. Life jackets were spotted, but no crew had been found, and the search was continuing. The second ship caught fire. Separately, a Russian drone hit a Marshall Islands-flagged ship carrying rapeseed oil off Ukraine, killing a steward and injuring seven crew members, Odesa Governor Oleh Kiper said. The strikes come days after a Turkish-owned grain ship sank off Romania in what Ukraine blamed on Russian drones.

stories.headline: Tesla registered just 993 cars in its first 13 months in India, but September set a record after a price cut and the six-seat Model Y L
stories.summary: Tesla has registered 993 vehicles in India since deliveries began in September 2025, according to registration data from Indian EV site ElecTree, with 294 of them in September 2026 alone, a record. In its first nine months Tesla sold only 428 cars, pricing its imported Model Y at roughly $70,000, and in May India confirmed Tesla will not build a factory there. Two moves changed the trend: the six-seat Model Y L launched in April at about $65,000, and in late May Tesla cut the base Model Y 15% to about $53,000. Since June it has registered 565 cars, and the Model Y L made up 81% of September’s total. Tesla is still under 1% of India’s fast-growing EV market, but it is now the No. 2 luxury EV brand there behind BMW. It has added showrooms in Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Chennai and Noida.

stories.headline: Judge adds $184 million in interest to Apple’s Apple Watch patent loss to Masimo, pushing the bill to about $818 million
stories.summary: A federal judge has ordered Apple to pay Masimo another $184 million in prejudgment interest on top of the $634 million a jury awarded in November 2025 over a Masimo pulse-oximetry patent, bringing Apple’s bill to about $818 million before post-judgment interest. Judge James Selna rejected Apple’s argument that interest would be a windfall, citing Supreme Court guidance that it simply makes a patent owner whole for royalties it should have received. Masimo did not get everything: Selna refused its request for a 7% rate, which would have meant $243 million, and used Masimo’s own borrowing rate instead. Masimo is also behind the separate fight that led to the U.S. import ban on some Apple Watch models and forced Apple to disable and later redesign the blood oxygen feature.

stories.headline: New code points to four-HomePod surround sound for the Apple TV 4K ahead of Apple’s Oct. 13 home launch
stories.summary: More evidence has turned up that Apple will let owners link four HomePods to an Apple TV 4K as front-left, front-right, rear-left and rear-right surround speakers. The leaker known as “pdfu,” who first reported Apple testing the setup last month, found more related code in the third audioOS 27.2 beta, including a line saying Siri can match a speaker to its surround system. MacRumors contributor Aaron Perris also found two new symbols in the third macOS 27.2 beta showing four speakers arranged in a room, one labeled as part of a home theater. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman says Apple plans to unveil a new HomePod mini and Apple TV 4K on Tuesday, Oct. 13. It is not yet clear whether surround sound will work with the HomePod mini or only the full-size HomePod.

stories.headline: LEGO opens pre-orders for BrickLink Designer Program Series 9 fan-designed sets through Oct. 12
stories.summary: The fan-designed BrickLink Designer Program Series 9 sets are now up for pre-order on the LEGO Shop until Oct. 12. The run is limited and production depends on demand: each set needs 3,000 pre-orders to be made and can be produced up to 30,000 times, and if one model falls short LEGO can shift extra production to the others. The sets will not ship until March 2027, and buyers are not charged until then.

stories.headline: Penguins after three games: Kindel, Carlile and Malkin impress, but seven third-period goals against are a red flag
stories.summary: PensBurgh’s Adam Gretz sorts out the 2-1 start: a near-flawless opener at Philadelphia, a 6-5 overtime win over Montreal after blowing a 5-1 lead, and Monday’s sloppy 3-2 loss to Winnipeg. Ben Kindel has two goals, both from the front of the net, plus an assist in two games, and looks “bigger, stronger and faster.” Defenseman Declan Carlile, signed as a possible Parker Wotherspoon replacement next to Erik Karlsson, already has a career-high four points. Evgeni Malkin was excellent in the first two games. On the worry list: seven third-period goals allowed in two games, a problem carried over from last season; Connor Dewar’s defensive-zone turnovers; and a power play that had no answer for Winnipeg’s aggressive penalty kill. The Penguins play at Washington on Wednesday.

stories.headline: Minkah Fitzpatrick’s 16-tackle, one-interception return in Chicago was the biggest tackling game of his career
stories.summary: In his first game back from two weeks out with a groin injury, safety Minkah Fitzpatrick played all 93 defensive snaps of Sunday’s 23-12 loss to the Bears and made 16 tackles, the most in his 126-game career. He had 10 tackles and his second-quarter interception in the first half alone, making him the first NFL safety since the Rams’ Eric Weddle in 2019 to put up 10 tackles and a pass defensed in a half, and the first Jets safety to do it in a first half since 1994. The pick was the 22nd of his career and ended the Jets’ interception drought. The team site’s stats rundown also credits the cornerbacks’ teamwork for limiting yardage and Stiggers for sharp kick coverage as the Jets turn to the Browns.

stories.headline: Dave Mustaine says Megadeth’s last album is still the last, but he’ll dig through leftover ‘half-songs’ from the sessions
stories.summary: In a Q&A before Megadeth’s Sept. 24 set at the Grammy Museum in Los Angeles, Dave Mustaine said he stands by his word that the band’s chart-topping 17th studio album will be its last, but more Megadeth music could still come out. He explained that new riffs keep coming during recording and often get tacked onto the end of song files. “I can’t tell you how many megabytes of riffs there are at the end of our songs,” he said. “At some point, we’re going to go back with this record and see all the half-songs that are there and see what we have. And maybe we’ll end up discovering some new songs that are left over from the sessions.”

stories.headline: Fender rolls out three John 5 signature Telecasters, bringing back the white ‘Ghost,’ and he drops a new song called ‘Phantom’
stories.summary: Fender and the Fender Custom Shop have announced three John 5 signature Telecasters at different price points. The black Phantom pairs DiMarzio D Activator humbuckers with a Floyd Rose Special Series tremolo, and has a single volume knob and a killswitch. The Arctic White Ghost, with a nyatoh body, red accents and the same pickups, brings the model back to Fender’s lineup. The top-end Custom Shop “Phantom” adds an alder body, a compound-radius ebony fingerboard, an original Floyd Rose double-locking tremolo and locking tuners. “Ever since I was little, Fender was always just the pinnacle,” John 5 said. He also released a new single and video, “Phantom,” the follow-up to his album “Ghost.”

stories.headline: Mudvayne’s Chad Gray reveals a hemorrhaged, swollen vocal fold: ‘To tell you I was scared would be the understatement of my life’
stories.summary: Mudvayne and Hellyeah singer Chad Gray told The Jesea Lee Show that a scope found one of his vocal folds is twice as wide as the other, with a large broken blood vessel showing he had hemorrhaged at some point. That forced him to cancel his San Diego and Santa Ana solo shows on Oct. 5 and 6. He first thought it was allergies during rehearsals in Nashville. “It’s not only my instrument — it’s my life, it’s my career,” Gray said. Doctors have not recommended surgery yet, but he expects he may need it, and for now he is on vocal rest. His “30 Years Of Madness” tour, with Butcher Babies and Devil’s Cut, is set to resume Oct. 7 at the Fremont Country Club in Las Vegas.

stories.headline: How to spend 72 hours in Palm Springs, from about 15,000 miles round trip out of New York
stories.summary: The Points Guy lays out a three-day Palm Springs weekend built around points. Alaska, American, Delta and United have added or extended service to the desert city, and award searches turned up New York round trips for about 15,000 United or 15,500 American miles, with cash fares from New York as low as $296. The writer stayed at the new Thompson Palm Springs by Hyatt on Palm Canyon Drive, with 168 rooms, two pools and an adults-only tower, bookable for 20,000 to 25,000 World of Hyatt points a night against cash rates from $285. Beyond pools and midcentury-modern house tours, the hotel sits next to downtown restaurants and attractions, and the guide notes that late fall into the holidays is prime season, when much of the country turns cold.

stories.headline: Fairfield County homeowners and businesses hit by the Sept. 13 flash flooding can now apply for low-interest SBA disaster loans
stories.summary: The U.S. Small Business Administration has approved a disaster declaration for the severe storms and flash flooding of Sept. 13. Fairfield County, which includes Trumbull, is the primary county in the federal notice published Tuesday, and neighboring Litchfield and New Haven counties are also eligible. Homeowners can borrow up to $500,000 to repair a primary home, homeowners and renters up to $100,000 for damaged belongings, and businesses and nonprofits up to $2 million for physical losses or working capital. The federal notice lists homeowner rates of 3% for those without credit elsewhere. An in-person SBA Disaster Loan Outreach Center opens Wednesday, Oct. 7, at the Margaret E. Morton Government Center, 999 Broad Street in Bridgeport. Applications are also taken at lending.sba.gov or 1-800-659-2955. The deadline for property-damage loans is Dec. 1.
